source.title: Do Neural Scaling Laws Exist on Graph Self-Supervised Learning?
source.authors: Qian Ma; Hai-Tao Mao; Jing-Zhe Liu; Zhehua Zhang; Chunlin Feng; Yu Song; Yihan Shao; Yao Ma

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling-like behavior in graph self-supervised learning, a modality and training setting beyond text language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper measures held-out graph SSL objectives and downstream performance across data and model scales. Its SSL objectives are not language-model cross-entropy, and it does not test language-model extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or downstream predictability from pretraining loss. It reports many additional figure results; the selected rows prioritize primary datasets and contrasting settings. Results cited from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study fits the power-law form (ε = aX^-b + ε∞) to held-out graph SSL loss and to downstream linear-probe performance. It varies pre-training data and encoder size (depth and width) for four graph SSL methods. This is a new modality and training regime with its own scaling results.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. More precisely: held-out SSL loss falls with more data and with more layers, but not with wider layers. Downstream performance merely fluctuates across data and model scales, which the authors attribute to a gap between SSL and downstream tasks. They trace loss gains to more aggregations rather than more parameters, and find contrastive methods scale more consistently than the generative GraphMAE.
record.recipe_differences: Graph self-supervised learning benchmark; varies graph dataset size and graph encoder architecture, and measures SSL objectives and downstream graph tasks rather than language-model cross-entropy or compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with SSL method, dataset, and scaling route: increasing layer count can lower SSL loss, while increasing hidden size at fixed depth does not show consistent SSL-loss scaling; data-scaling consistency differs by method.

fits_no_version.finding: InfoGraph1T decouples aggregation from transformation. Its held-out SSL loss scales with the number of message-passing aggregations, without added learnable parameters, almost overlapping the original InfoGraph (Fig. 13).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In graph SSL, loss gains with depth come from more aggregation steps rather than parameter count.

record.problems: The paper reports curve plots and R2 fit-quality statistics rather than uncertainty estimates or tabulated loss values. It states that downstream metrics vary only marginally in some cases. The held-out SSL objectives and graph tasks are not language-model cross-entropy or language-model downstream evaluations.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted additional figure results under the 60-row cap: data-scaling results for ogbg-molpcba and ZINC-Full (Figures 14-17); further model-scaling downstream and SSL-loss sweeps for ogbg-molpcba, ogbg-ppa, and ZINC-Full (Figures 18-29); and the augmentation-setting experiments in Appendix E. These are described as largely consistent with the reported patterns, with some method- and setting-specific differences.

untested.parts: Image/video and other non-graph modalities; repeated data; fine-tuning. Data scaling spans only about one order of magnitude (ratio 0.1–1), so 'several orders of magnitude' for data is untested. Compute scaling is not tested, and no exponents are reported.
Language-model downstream tasks; prediction of downstream performance from pretraining loss via a fitted mapping.
No extrapolation to larger runs is attempted.
The depth vs width comparisons do not hold parameter count fixed.
No comparison of fitting methods or of published laws.

missing.what: Downstream performance vs hidden size at fixed layer count. R2: GraphCL 0.56, JOAO 0.79, InfoGraph 0.49, GraphMAE 0.64 on reddit-threads; 0.0, 0.0, 0.11, 0.18 on ogbg-molhiv. The authors report no consistent scaling.
InfoGraph1T vs InfoGraph: SSL loss vs number of aggregations (nhid=96) on three datasets.

record.verdict_notes: The downstream rows are linked to V6 on the reading that V6 does not restrict the system type; if V6 is LM-only, these rows bear on V5 (transfer) instead. R2 is fit quality, not evidence of a slope; the authors stress this. No exponents, uncertainties or tabulated values are reported. Rows_left_out declares Figs 14–29, which include counterexamples: ogbg-molpcba data scaling of SSL loss gives JOAO R2 0.01 and GraphMAE 0.0; ogbg-molpcba layer scaling gives GraphMAE 0.17. Preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling against parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger language-model runs from smaller-run fits.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Whether architecture details change loss only slightly at a fixed parameter count; the reported graph comparisons do not isolate fixed parameter count.
Image/video and other non-graph modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer; language-model cross-entropy specifically.
Whether downstream performance is predictable from pretraining loss; the paper varies scales and reports downstream results but does not test loss-to-performance prediction.
Dependence of language-model exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices and the disagreement of published language-model laws.
